subject: Architects sync — finding an overlap window for technical deep-dive
messages:
From: Rana Cho <rana.cho@atlasbank.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@atlasbank.com>, archs@atlasbank.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:11:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — technical deep-dive request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for last week's overview — the execs liked the cost/latency numbers. Our architects (Miguel and the "archs@" alias) want a focused technical deep-dive next week to validate network egress, KV caching behavior for long conversations, and planned rollout patterns. We need Solutions + our infra leads in the same call. The challenge: our team is split across NYC (EST), Madrid (CET), and Bengaluru (IST).

Can you propose a couple of 60–75 minute windows that have at least one hour of useful overlap for all three regions? We prefer mornings in Bangalore if possible — the architects are flexible but can only do afternoons CET after 1500 CET. Also FYI, the US DST change is mid-March which might affect recurring invites.

Would appreciate 3 options and an agenda.

— Rana
Director, Infrastructure
Atlas Bank

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Rana Cho <rana.cho@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@atlasbank.com>, archs@atlasbank.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — technical deep-dive request

Hi Rana — thanks, this is great context.

Quick answers up front: we can do a 60–75 min session focused on KV cache, batching, network egress patterns and a short live run of a 20-min simulated long-conversation. I attached a proposed agenda (agenda-architects.pdf) and a rough infra sketch.

Below are three candidate windows (local times shown). Note the US DST starts Sun Mar 14; that will shift EST->EDT (UTC-4) which affects recurring invites after that date. I call out UTC times too so you can map on your side.

Option A (preferred) — early Bangalore / late Madrid
- 2027-03-08 08:30 IST / 04:00 CET / 23:30 EDT (previous day) — 60 min (UTC 03:00)
Option B — mid-overlap (UTC-friendly)
- 2027-03-09 14:00 CET / 09:30 IST / 08:00 EDT — 75 min (UTC 13:00)
Option C — US-friendly (later EU afternoon)
- 2027-03-10 16:00 CET / 20:30 IST / 11:00 EDT — 60 min (UTC 15:00)

Notes:
- Option A is tight for Madrid (04:00 CET) but gives Bangalore a friendly morning and keeps US late-night — only do A if Madrid can stretch early.
- Option B is generally the cleanest cross-over (midday CET, morning IST, morning US).
- Option C moves EU later in their afternoon for more convenience for Madrid.

Karthik / Soojin — can you confirm SE/ENG availability for these slots? Also flag any concerns with the agenda (I attached infra-sketch.png).

Rana — if you prefer, pick 2 options and I'll send a calendar poll + meeting doc.

Thanks,
Tessa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — technical deep-dive request

Tessa — quick checklist from infra side. I've sketched overlap windows in UTC and converted to the main locales (rounding to 30-min). Keep DST in mind: US moves Mar 14 (UTC-5->UTC-4), EU moves Mar 28 (UTC+1->UTC+2). If this is a one-off event before March 14 we're fine; if recurring, pick slots after both changes or include explicit timezone in the invite (use UTC).

Practical overlap table (UTC-centric):
- 03:00–04:30 UTC -> IST 08:30–10:00 / CET 04:00–05:30 / EDT 23:00–00:30 (prev day) — good for early IST but bad for CET.
- 13:00–14:30 UTC -> IST 18:30–20:00 / CET 14:00–15:30 / EDT 09:00–10:30 — balanced, best for deep technical work.
- 15:00–16:00 UTC -> IST 20:30–21:30 / CET 16:00–17:00 / EDT 10:00–11:00 — EU late afternoon, US mid-morning, IST late evening.

For our SEs: I can cover Option B (13:00 UTC) and Option C (15:00 UTC) on the proposed dates. Option A is doable if Miguel confirms early CET.

Also: let's avoid scheduling across the Mar 14 DST boundary for a recurring series; if Atlas wants weekly follow-ups, suggest weekly at 13:00 UTC starting after Mar 28 to avoid double-shifts.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:41:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — technical deep-dive request

Thanks — I can take the run of the simulation and lead KV-cache discussion. Prefer Option B (13:00 UTC on Mar 09) or Option C (15:00 UTC on Mar 10). Option B is nicer for our engineering schedule (earlier in the day).

One practical ask: if Miguel / Rana want Bangalore morning, Option B maps to 18:30 IST (a little late for Bangalore). Option C (20:30 IST) is quite late for them. If they require a true morning IST slot, Option A is the only one that meets that requirement, but it is harsh on Madrid.

Recommendation to Rana: pick 2 options (B + C) and we mark Option A as fallback only if Madrid confirms early.

-Soojin
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Rana Cho <rana.cho@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@atlasbank.com>, archs@atlasbank.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:16:00 -0500
Subject: Proposed times + calendar poll — Architects technical deep-dive

Hi Rana — per internal checks we recommend two primary options and one fallback:

Option 1 (recommended): 2027-03-09 14:00 CET / 09:30 IST / 08:00 EDT — 75 min (UTC 13:00)
Option 2: 2027-03-10 16:00 CET / 20:30 IST / 11:00 EDT — 60 min (UTC 15:00)
Fallback: 2027-03-08 04:00 CET / 08:30 IST / 23:30 EDT (prev day) — only if Madrid can do an early start.

I created a quick calendar poll here: https://cal.redwood.com/s/tessa/atl-deep-dive. Please select preferred slots; if none work, reply with a narrow set of times and we'll iterate. I've attached the agenda and an infra sketch to help your architects prioritize topics.

Also confirming: we'll call out timezone explicitly in the invite in UTC to avoid DST ambiguity.

Cheers,
Tessa

--- Attachment stubs: agenda-architects.pdf (1 page), infra-sketch.png (PNG 800x600)

From: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@atlasbank.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Rana Cho <rana.cho@atlasbank.com>, archs@atlasbank.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed times + calendar poll — Architects technical deep-dive

Tessa — thanks for the clear options. Madrid prefers Option 1 (Mar 9 at 14:00 CET) but Miguel here — slight change: we have a procurement review that conflicts by 30 minutes. Can we shift Option 1 by +30 minutes so the session starts 14:30 CET / 09:00 IST / 08:30 EDT (UTC 13:30) and keep it to 60–75 min? That gives our Madrid folks time to hop from the review.

If that works for Redwood, please update the invite and confirm the final start in UTC in the body (so all calendars pick up UTC explicitly).

— Miguel
Lead Architect, Atlas Bank
